study_identification_part.si4_title: Judged by your neighbors: A novel framework for personalized assessment of brain structural aging effects in diverse populations

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Introduce Nearest Neighbor Normativity (N^3) to provide individualized brain structural normativity assessments that disentangle inter-individual variability from pathological alterations, and benchmark against traditional z-score-based normative modeling and brain age across neurodegenerative cohorts.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper explicitly states that after excluding age groups below 22 and above 72 years, the final training sample consisted of 29,883 individuals from NAKO. This is the number used for model training.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: The training data for fitting models of the different normative modeling approaches comprised 30,047 samples from the population-based NAKO cohort (for details see below). We exclude age groups below 22 years and above 72 years due to small sample sizes (n < 100), which restricts the final sample to 29,883.

rci3_hc_age.reason: The paper provides the mean and SD for the NAKO cohort in Table 2 (48.45 ± 12.09). The age range (22-72 years) is explicitly stated as the inclusion criteria in the Methods section.
rci3_hc_age.supporting_text: NAKO HC 29883 48.45 ± 12.09 (from Table 2); Exclusion criteria were applied based on age; participants younger than 22 years or older than 72 were omitted from the study, due to insufficient sample sizes in the normative reference sample.

rci4_hc_sex.reason: Table 2 provides detailed sex distribution for NAKO cohort, showing 13201 females (44.18%). The number of males can be calculated as 29883 - 13201 = 16682 (55.82%).

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: All neuroimaging data used are T1-weighted MRI scans.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: All neuroimaging data utilized in this study were T1-weighted MRI scans from these baseline measurements.

caa2_diseases_studied.answer: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI); Alzheimer's Disease (AD); Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD)
caa2_diseases_studied.reason: Diseases explicitly listed as model conditions to represent pathological deviations.
caa2_diseases_studied.supporting_text: ...Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) serve as model diseases...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: N^3 outperforms brain age and conventional z-score-based normative metrics in distinguishing AD and FTD and shows modest advantages for MCI; improves single-subject classification metrics across disorders.
